text: Explain the difference between SQL and NoSQL databases.
idealAnswer: SQL databases are relational, use structured schema, support ACID transactions, and are best for structured data with complex relationships. NoSQL databases are non-relational, offer flexible schema, scale horizontally, and are better for unstructured data and high throughput.

text: What is the difference between GET and POST HTTP methods?
idealAnswer: GET requests data from a server, parameters are in URL, is cacheable, and has length limitations. POST sends data to a server, parameters are in body, is not cacheable, and has no length limitations. GET should be idempotent while POST is not.

text: Explain the concept of polymorphism in object-oriented programming.
idealAnswer: Polymorphism allows objects of different classes to be treated as objects of a common superclass. It enables methods to do different things based on the object it is acting upon. Types include method overloading (compile-time) and method overriding (runtime).

text: What is the difference between process and thread?
idealAnswer: A process is a program in execution with its own memory space, resources, and address space. Threads are lightweight units within a process that share the same memory space and resources but have separate execution paths. Processes are isolated while threads within a process share memory.

text: Explain the concept of Big O notation.
idealAnswer: Big O notation describes the upper bound of an algorithm's time or space complexity as input size grows. It helps analyze algorithm efficiency by focusing on the worst-case scenario. Common complexities include O(1), O(log n), O(n), O(n log n), O(n²), and O(2ⁿ).

text: What is the difference between TCP and UDP?
idealAnswer: TCP is connection-oriented, reliable, ordered, and has error checking with flow control. UDP is connectionless, unreliable, unordered, has no error checking, but is faster with lower overhead. TCP is used for web browsing, email, file transfers. UDP is used for streaming, gaming, DNS.

text: Explain the concept of encapsulation in OOP.
idealAnswer: Encapsulation is the bundling of data and methods that operate on that data within a single unit (class). It hides internal state and requires interaction through well-defined interfaces. This provides data protection, reduces complexity, and allows implementation changes without affecting external code.

text: What is a RESTful API?
idealAnswer: RESTful API is an architectural style for designing networked applications using HTTP requests to access and manipulate data. It follows REST principles: stateless communication, resource-based URLs, standard HTTP methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE), and uses standard data formats like JSON.

text: Explain the difference between stack and queue data structures.
idealAnswer: Stack is LIFO (Last In First Out) - elements are added and removed from the same end (top). Queue is FIFO (First In First Out) - elements are added at rear and removed from front. Stack operations: push, pop, peek. Queue operations: enqueue, dequeue, peek.

text: What is the difference between authentication and authorization?
idealAnswer: Authentication verifies who a user is (identity) through credentials like passwords, biometrics, or tokens. Authorization determines what an authenticated user can do (permissions) based on roles, policies, or access rules. Authentication comes first, then authorization.

text: Explain the concept of inheritance in object-oriented programming.
idealAnswer: Inheritance allows a class to acquire properties and methods from another class (parent/superclass). It promotes code reuse, establishes hierarchical relationships, and enables polymorphism. Types include single inheritance, multiple inheritance, multilevel inheritance, and hierarchical inheritance.

text: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous programming?
idealAnswer: Synchronous code executes sequentially, blocking further execution until completion. Asynchronous code allows execution to continue while waiting for operations, using callbacks, promises, or async/await. Async is better for I/O operations, network requests, and preventing UI blocking.

text: Explain the concept of indexing in databases.
idealAnswer: Database indexes are data structures that improve query speed by allowing fast data retrieval without scanning entire tables. They work like book indexes, pointing to data locations. Types include B-tree, hash, and full-text indexes. Trade-offs include increased storage and slower write operations.

text: What is the difference between monolithic and microservices architecture?
idealAnswer: Monolithic architecture has all functionality in a single deployable unit, simpler to develop initially but harder to scale and maintain. Microservices break applications into small, independent services that communicate via APIs, offering better scalability, fault isolation, and technology flexibility but with increased complexity.

text: Explain the concept of recursion in programming.
idealAnswer: Recursion is a programming technique where a function calls itself to solve smaller instances of the same problem. It requires a base case to terminate and recursive case to break down the problem. Common uses include tree traversal, divide and conquer algorithms, and mathematical computations.

text: What is the difference between HTTP and HTTPS?
idealAnswer: HTTP is unencrypted, sends data in plain text, uses port 80. HTTPS encrypts data using SSL/TLS, provides secure communication, uses port 443. HTTPS protects against eavesdropping, tampering, and man-in-the-middle attacks. HTTPS requires SSL certificates.

text: Explain the concept of normalization in databases.
idealAnswer: Normalization is the process of organizing data to reduce redundancy and improve data integrity. It involves dividing databases into tables and establishing relationships. Normal forms (1NF, 2NF, 3NF, BCNF) provide rules for eliminating dependencies and anomalies. Trade-offs include query complexity.

text: What is the difference between abstract class and interface?
idealAnswer: Abstract class can have both abstract and concrete methods, can have instance variables, supports constructors, and single inheritance. Interface only has abstract methods, no instance variables, no constructors, and supports multiple implementation. Abstract classes share code, interfaces define contracts.

text: Explain the concept of load balancing in system design.
idealAnswer: Load balancing distributes incoming network traffic across multiple servers to ensure no single server bears too much demand. It improves responsiveness, availability, and reliability. Algorithms include round robin, least connections, IP hash. Can be implemented with hardware or software solutions.

text: What is the difference between primary key and unique key?
idealAnswer: Primary key uniquely identifies each record, cannot be null, only one per table. Unique key ensures uniqueness but can be null, multiple unique keys allowed per table. Both enforce uniqueness but primary key is the main identifier while unique keys are additional constraints.

text: Explain the concept of caching in system design.
idealAnswer: Caching stores frequently accessed data in fast storage to reduce latency and database load. Types include browser cache, CDN cache, database cache, application cache. Cache eviction policies include LRU, LFU, FIFO. Challenges include cache invalidation, consistency, and stale data.

text: What is the difference between shallow copy and deep copy?
idealAnswer: Shallow copy copies the object structure but nested objects are still referenced. Deep copy creates completely independent copies including nested objects. Shallow copy is faster but shares references. Deep copy is slower but creates true independence. Implementation varies by language.

text: Explain the concept of database transactions and ACID properties.
idealAnswer: Database transactions are sequences of operations treated as a single unit of work. ACID properties ensure reliability: Atomicity (all or nothing), Consistency (database remains valid), Isolation (transactions don't interfere), Durability (committed transactions persist). Essential for financial and critical operations.

text: What is the difference between SQL joins: INNER, LEFT, RIGHT, FULL?
idealAnswer: INNER JOIN returns rows with matching values in both tables. LEFT JOIN returns all rows from left table and matching from right (null if no match). RIGHT JOIN returns all rows from right table and matching from left (null if no match). FULL JOIN returns all rows when there's a match in either table.

text: Explain the concept of message queues in system design.
idealAnswer: Message queues enable asynchronous communication between services by storing messages temporarily. They decouple producers and consumers, handle varying processing rates, and provide fault tolerance. Common implementations include RabbitMQ, Kafka, AWS SQS. Patterns include point-to-point and publish-subscribe.

text: What is the difference between array and linked list?
idealAnswer: Arrays have contiguous memory, O(1) random access, fixed size, efficient iteration. Linked lists have non-contiguous memory, O(n) access, dynamic size, efficient insertion/deletion. Arrays use less memory per element. Linked lists require extra memory for pointers. Choice depends on use case.

text: Explain the concept of dependency injection.
idealAnswer: Dependency injection is a design pattern where dependencies are provided to a class rather than created internally. It promotes loose coupling, easier testing, and better maintainability. Types include constructor injection, setter injection, and interface injection. Commonly used in frameworks like Spring and Angular.

text: What is the difference between NoSQL document stores and key-value stores?
idealAnswer: Document stores (MongoDB) store data in flexible JSON-like documents with nested structures, support complex queries, and are schema-less. Key-value stores (Redis) store simple key-value pairs, offer extremely fast performance, but have limited query capabilities. Document stores for complex data, key-value for caching and simple lookups.

text: Explain the concept of horizontal vs vertical scaling.
idealAnswer: Vertical scaling adds more resources (CPU, RAM) to a single server. Simpler but has limits and single point of failure. Horizontal scaling adds more servers to distribute load. More complex but offers unlimited scaling and better fault tolerance. Cloud environments favor horizontal scaling.

text: What is the difference between cookie and session?
idealAnswer: Cookies are small text files stored on client browser, sent with HTTP requests, have size limits, can be persistent. Sessions are server-side storage of user data, identified by session ID (often stored in cookie), more secure, no size limits. Cookies for client storage, sessions for server-side state.

text: Explain the concept of database sharding.
idealAnswer: Sharding partitions a large database across multiple servers (shards) based on a shard key. Each shard holds a subset of data. Improves scalability and performance but adds complexity for queries, transactions, and rebalancing. Common strategies include range-based, hash-based, and directory-based sharding.

text: What is the difference between GraphQL and REST?
idealAnswer: REST uses multiple endpoints for different resources, over-fetching/under-fetching data, HTTP methods define operations. GraphQL uses single endpoint, clients specify exact data needed, strongly typed schema, real-time subscriptions. REST simpler for caching, GraphQL more flexible for complex data requirements.

text: Explain the concept of database replication.
idealAnswer: Database replication copies data from a primary database to one or more replicas. Improves read performance, provides fault tolerance, and enables disaster recovery. Types include master-slave (one-way), master-master (bi-directional), and multi-master. Challenges include consistency, latency, and conflict resolution.

text: What is the difference between compiler and interpreter?
idealAnswer: Compiler translates entire source code to machine code before execution, produces executable file, faster execution, better optimization. Interpreter translates and executes line by line, no executable file, slower execution, easier debugging. Some languages use both (JIT compilation).

text: Explain the concept of microservices communication patterns.
idealAnswer: Microservices communicate via synchronous (REST, gRPC) or asynchronous (message queues, event streaming) patterns. Synchronous is simpler but creates coupling. Asynchronous provides decoupling and reliability. Service mesh handles communication complexity. API gateways provide single entry point. Event-driven architecture enables loose coupling.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL when to use each?
idealAnswer: Use SQL when data structure is well-defined, relationships are complex, ACID transactions required, data consistency critical. Use NoSQL when data structure is flexible or evolving, high write throughput needed, horizontal scaling required, unstructured data. SQL for traditional applications, NoSQL for big data, real-time apps, and rapid prototyping.

text: Explain the concept of API rate limiting.
idealAnswer: API rate limiting controls the number of requests a client can make in a time period. Prevents abuse, ensures fair usage, and protects system resources. Algorithms include token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window, and sliding window. Can be implemented at API gateway, application level, or using reverse proxies.

text: What is the difference between stateful and stateless applications?
idealAnswer: Stateful applications maintain client context between requests, store session data, harder to scale, require sticky sessions. Stateless applications don't maintain context, each request independent, easier to scale horizontally, require external session storage. Modern architectures favor stateless for scalability and reliability.

text: Explain the concept of database connection pooling.
idealAnswer: Connection pooling maintains a cache of database connections to reuse for multiple requests. Reduces overhead of creating new connections, improves performance, and limits resource usage. Pool size configuration balances performance and resource consumption. Common in web applications and ORM frameworks.

text: What is the difference between monolithic and serverless architecture?
idealAnswer: Monolithic runs continuously on servers, you manage infrastructure, predictable costs, easier debugging. Serverless runs on-demand in functions, cloud manages infrastructure, pay-per-use, automatic scaling. Monolithic for stable workloads, serverless for sporadic traffic and rapid development. Serverless has cold starts and vendor lock-in.

text: Explain the concept of API versioning strategies.
idealAnswer: API versioning manages changes without breaking existing clients. Strategies include URL versioning (/v1/resource), header versioning (Accept: application/vnd.api.v1+json), query parameter versioning (?version=1), and content negotiation. Each has trade-offs in caching, implementation complexity, and client experience.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data models?
idealAnswer: SQL uses relational model with tables, rows, columns, and predefined schemas. Enforces data integrity through constraints. NoSQL offers various models: document (JSON-like), key-value, column-family, and graph. More flexible schemas, better for unstructured data. SQL for structured data with relationships, NoSQL for flexible and hierarchical data.

text: Explain the concept of eventual consistency in distributed systems.
idealAnswer: Eventual consistency guarantees that if no new updates are made, eventually all accesses will return the last updated value. Used in distributed systems where immediate consistency is impractical. Trade-offs include temporary inconsistencies and complex conflict resolution. Common in NoSQL databases and CDN systems.

text: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous replication?
idealAnswer: Synchronous replication waits for acknowledgment from all replicas before confirming write, ensures strong consistency but slower performance. Asynchronous replication confirms write immediately, replicates in background, faster performance but risk of data loss if primary fails. Choice depends on consistency vs performance requirements.

text: Explain the concept of API authentication methods.
idealAnswer: API authentication methods include API keys (simple but less secure), OAuth 2.0 (industry standard for delegated access), JWT (stateless tokens), Basic Auth (username/password), and mutual TLS (certificate-based). Choice depends on security requirements, use case, and implementation complexity. OAuth 2.0 and JWT are most common.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL scaling?
idealAnswer: SQL databases traditionally scale vertically (bigger servers), though some support horizontal scaling with complexity. NoSQL databases designed for horizontal scaling across commodity servers. SQL scaling limited by single-server constraints. NoSQL scales better for large datasets and high throughput but may sacrifice some consistency features.

text: Explain the concept of database indexing strategies.
idealAnswer: Indexing strategies include B-tree indexes (range queries, equality), hash indexes (equality only), composite indexes (multiple columns), covering indexes (include all needed columns), and partial indexes (subset of data). Choice depends on query patterns, read/write ratios, and storage constraints. Over-indexing slows writes.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL query languages?
idealAnswer: SQL uses standardized declarative language (SELECT, INSERT, UPDATE) with JOINs for relational data. NoSQL query languages vary by type: document stores use JSON-like queries, key-value stores use simple key access, column-family uses Cassandra Query Language, graph databases use graph traversal languages. SQL is more standardized, NoSQL varies by implementation.

text: Explain the concept of API security best practices.
idealAnswer: API security best practices include using HTTPS, implementing proper authentication and authorization, rate limiting, input validation, output encoding, using security headers (CORS, CSP), logging and monitoring, and keeping dependencies updated. Defense in depth approach with multiple security layers.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL transaction support?
idealAnswer: SQL databases provide full ACID transaction support across multiple operations and tables. NoSQL transaction support varies: some document databases support multi-document transactions, key-value stores often limited to single-key operations, distributed databases offer eventual consistency. SQL for complex transactions, NoSQL may sacrifice ACID for performance and scalability.

text: Explain the concept of API documentation tools.
idealAnswer: API documentation tools include Swagger/OpenAPI (interactive documentation, code generation), Postman (testing and documentation), API Blueprint (Markdown-based), and RAML (RESTful API Modeling Language). Tools help create, maintain, and share API documentation, improving developer experience and API adoption.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL schema flexibility?
idealAnswer: SQL databases require predefined schema with fixed columns and types, schema changes are expensive and require migrations. NoSQL databases offer schema flexibility, can store varying structures, evolve schema without downtime. SQL for stable data structures, NoSQL for evolving or heterogeneous data. Schema flexibility vs data integrity trade-off.

text: Explain the concept of API testing strategies.
idealAnswer: API testing strategies include unit testing (individual endpoints), integration testing (API interactions), contract testing (API compliance), performance testing (load and stress), and security testing (vulnerabilities). Tools include Postman, JMeter, SoapUI. Automated testing in CI/CD ensures API reliability and performance.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data consistency models?
idealAnswer: SQL databases typically offer strong consistency (immediate, all nodes see same data). NoSQL databases offer various consistency models: strong, eventual, causal, and tunable consistency. Trade-offs between consistency, availability, and partition tolerance (CAP theorem). SQL for immediate consistency, NoSQL for availability and partition tolerance.

text: Explain the concept of API gateway patterns.
idealAnswer: API gateway patterns include single entry point, request routing, composition (aggregating multiple service calls), protocol translation, and cross-cutting concerns (authentication, rate limiting). Simplifies client interaction, provides security, and handles traffic management. Popular implementations include Kong, AWS API Gateway, and Netflix Zuul.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL use cases?
idealAnswer: SQL use cases: financial systems, inventory management, CRM, applications requiring complex queries and relationships. NoSQL use cases: real-time big data, content management, social networks, IoT data, rapid prototyping. SQL for structured, relational data with consistency requirements. NoSQL for flexible, high-volume, distributed data.

text: Explain the concept of API monitoring and observability.
idealAnswer: API monitoring tracks metrics (response time, error rates, throughput), logging captures events, tracing follows requests across services. Tools include Prometheus, Grafana, ELK stack, Jaeger. Observability combines monitoring, logging, and tracing to understand system behavior, debug issues, and ensure performance.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL deployment models?
idealAnswer: SQL databases often deployed on dedicated servers or managed services with vertical scaling focus. NoSQL databases designed for distributed deployment across clusters, horizontal scaling, and cloud-native environments. SQL deployment simpler initially, NoSQL better for cloud and distributed architectures. Both available as managed cloud services.

text: Explain the concept of API design principles.
idealAnswer: API design principles include using nouns for resources, plural names, consistent naming conventions, appropriate HTTP methods, status codes, pagination, filtering, sorting, versioning, and comprehensive documentation. Good API design improves developer experience, reduces integration complexity, and ensures long-term maintainability.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL backup and recovery?
idealAnswer: SQL backup typically involves full database dumps, transaction logs, point-in-time recovery. NoSQL backup varies: document stores use snapshots, key-value stores use key-level backup, distributed systems use replica-based recovery. SQL backup more standardized, NoSQL backup depends on implementation and data model.

text: Explain the concept of API rate limiting algorithms.
idealAnswer: Rate limiting algorithms include token bucket (fixed capacity, tokens replenish over time), leaky bucket (fixed rate, requests leak out), fixed window (reset counter after time period), and sliding window (more accurate tracking). Choice depends on desired traffic shape, implementation complexity, and accuracy requirements.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL cost structures?
idealAnswer: SQL databases often have higher upfront costs for hardware and licensing, predictable scaling costs. NoSQL databases designed for commodity hardware, lower initial costs, but operational complexity can increase costs. Cloud services offer pay-as-you-go for both. Total cost depends on workload, scaling requirements, and operational expertise.

text: Explain the concept of API error handling strategies.
idealAnswer: API error handling includes using appropriate HTTP status codes (4xx for client errors, 5xx for server errors), consistent error response formats, detailed error messages, error codes for programmatic handling, and logging for debugging. Good error handling improves developer experience and debugging capability.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL community and ecosystem?
idealAnswer: SQL has mature ecosystem, standardized language, many tools, extensive documentation, and large talent pool. NoSQL ecosystem is newer, more fragmented with different implementations, rapidly evolving tools, and smaller but growing talent pool. SQL benefits from decades of development, NoSQL from innovation and cloud-native design.

text: Explain the concept of API pagination strategies.
idealAnswer: Pagination strategies include offset-based (page number and size), cursor-based (opaque cursor for position), keyset pagination (use last seen value), and time-based pagination. Cursor-based is better for large datasets and real-time data. Choice depends on data characteristics and performance requirements.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL learning curve?
idealAnswer: SQL has standardized language, many learning resources, and concepts transfer across implementations. NoSQL has varying query languages and concepts per database type, less standardization, but often simpler for basic operations. SQL easier to learn fundamentals, NoSQL requires learning specific database characteristics and patterns.

text: Explain the concept of API caching strategies.
idealAnswer: API caching strategies include client-side caching (browser cache), CDN caching (edge caching), application caching (Redis, Memcached), and database query caching. Cache invalidation strategies include time-based, event-based, and manual. Caching reduces latency, server load, and improves scalability but adds complexity.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data modeling?
idealAnswer: SQL data modeling focuses on normalization, reducing redundancy, defining relationships through foreign keys. NoSQL data modeling emphasizes denormalization, embedding related data, optimizing for read/write patterns. SQL modeling for data integrity, NoSQL for performance and query patterns. Different mindsets for data structure design.

text: Explain the concept of API security headers.
idealAnswer: API security headers include CORS (Cross-Origin Resource Sharing), CSP (Content Security Policy), X-Frame-Options (clickjacking protection), X-Content-Type-Options (MIME sniffing protection), Strict-Transport-Security (HTTPS enforcement), and X-XSS-Protection (XSS filtering). Headers protect against various web vulnerabilities and attacks.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL maturity and stability?
idealAnswer: SQL databases are mature, stable, with proven reliability over decades. NoSQL databases are newer, rapidly evolving, with frequent updates and changing features. SQL for mission-critical stability, NoSQL for innovation and modern use cases. SQL offers predictable behavior, NoSQL offers cutting-edge features.

text: Explain the concept of API versioning deprecation strategies.
idealAnswer: API version deprecation strategies include sunset headers (warning about deprecation), grace periods (time to migrate), migration guides, automatic redirects, and feature flags. Communication through documentation, email notifications, and status pages. Smooth deprecation requires planning and developer communication.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL vendor lock-in?
idealAnswer: SQL has standard language and concepts, reducing vendor lock-in, though implementations have proprietary features. NoSQL has less standardization, more vendor-specific features and query languages, increasing lock-in risk. SQL easier to migrate between vendors, NoSQL migration more challenging due to implementation differences.

text: Explain the concept of API load testing.
idealAnswer: API load testing simulates expected traffic to measure performance, identify bottlenecks, and determine capacity. Tools include JMeter, Gatling, k6. Metrics include response time, throughput, error rates, and resource utilization. Regular load testing ensures APIs can handle production traffic and helps with capacity planning.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data integrity?
idealAnswer: SQL databases enforce data integrity through constraints (primary key, foreign key, unique, check), transactions, and referential integrity. NoSQL databases offer limited integrity enforcement, often relying on application-level validation. SQL for strong data integrity, NoSQL trades integrity for flexibility and performance.

text: Explain the concept of API documentation standards.
idealAnswer: API documentation standards include OpenAPI/Swagger (comprehensive spec), API Blueprint (Markdown-based), RAML (RESTful API Modeling Language), and JSON Schema. Standards enable documentation generation, client SDK creation, and API testing. Good documentation includes endpoints, parameters, responses, examples, and authentication.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL query performance?
idealAnswer: SQL query performance optimized through indexes, query optimization, and execution plans. NoSQL query performance varies: key-value extremely fast for key lookups, document stores good for nested queries, graph databases excellent for relationship queries. SQL for complex queries, NoSQL for specific access patterns and high throughput.

text: Explain the concept of API security testing.
idealAnswer: API security testing includes penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, authentication testing, input validation testing, and authorization testing. Tools include OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite, Postman security features. Regular security testing identifies vulnerabilities like injection attacks, broken authentication, and data exposure.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL horizontal scaling?
idealAnswer: SQL horizontal scaling achieved through sharding, read replicas, and clustering, but complex to implement and maintain. NoSQL designed for horizontal scaling with built-in sharding, replication, and automatic distribution. SQL scaling possible but requires expertise, NoSQL scaling simpler by design. Both benefit from cloud managed services.

text: Explain the concept of API governance.
idealAnswer: API governance includes policies for API design, security, versioning, documentation, and lifecycle management. Ensures consistency across APIs, compliance with standards, and proper deprecation processes. Tools include API gateways, API management platforms, and governance frameworks. Governance improves API quality and developer experience.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data relationships?
idealAnswer: SQL uses foreign keys to define relationships between tables, supports complex JOINs, enforces referential integrity. NoSQL handles relationships differently: document databases embed related data or use manual references, graph databases designed for relationships, key-value stores minimal relationship support. SQL for complex relationships, NoSQL for embedded or graph-based relationships.

text: Explain the concept of API mocking for development.
idealAnswer: API mocking simulates API responses for development and testing without real backend. Tools include Postman Mock Server, JSON Server, WireMock, and Prism. Benefits include parallel development, testing edge cases, and offline development. Mocking should match real API contracts and be updated when APIs change.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL backup complexity?
idealAnswer: SQL backup more standardized with well-established tools and procedures for consistent backups and point-in-time recovery. NoSQL backup varies by database type and implementation, some require different approaches for different data models. SQL backup processes more mature, NoSQL backup may require custom solutions depending on database.

text: Explain the concept of API lifecycle management.
idealAnswer: API lifecycle management includes planning, design, development, testing, deployment, versioning, monitoring, and deprecation. Each phase requires specific processes and tools. Proper lifecycle management ensures API quality, security, and maintainability throughout its existence. API management platforms support lifecycle automation.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data migration?
idealAnswer: SQL data migration uses standardized ETL tools, schema mapping, and transformation scripts. NoSQL data migration varies by data model, may require custom transformation logic, and different tools for different database types. SQL migration more standardized, NoSQL migration depends on source and target database characteristics.

text: Explain the concept of API rate limiting implementation.
idealAnswer: Rate limiting implementation can be at API gateway, application level, or using reverse proxies. Storage options include in-memory (Redis), distributed caches, or databases. Considerations include distributed systems consistency, performance impact, and configuration flexibility. Implementation choice depends on architecture and requirements.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data validation?
idealAnswer: SQL databases provide built-in data validation through constraints, data types, and triggers. NoSQL databases offer limited built-in validation, often relying on application-level validation or document schema validation. SQL for database-enforced validation, NoSQL for application-level validation flexibility. Validation approach affects data quality.

text: Explain the concept of API monitoring metrics.
idealAnswer: API monitoring metrics include request rate, response time (p50, p95, p99), error rate, throughput, latency distribution, and resource utilization. Custom metrics track business-specific KPIs. Metrics collection uses tools like Prometheus, Datadog, or cloud monitoring services. Alerting based on metric thresholds ensures proactive issue detection.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data partitioning?
idealAnswer: SQL partitioning divides large tables into smaller, more manageable pieces based on ranges, lists, or hashes. NoSQL partitioning (sharding) distributes data across servers based on shard keys. SQL partitioning within single database, NoSQL sharding across distributed systems. Both improve query performance and manageability but at different scales.

text: Explain the concept of API security best practices for authentication.
idealAnswer: API authentication best practices include using industry-standard protocols (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect), implementing token expiration and refresh, using secure token storage, multi-factor authentication for sensitive operations, and regularly rotating secrets. Avoid basic auth in production, use HTTPS always, and implement proper session management.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data archiving?
idealAnswer: SQL data archiving moves old data to separate tables or databases, maintaining schema consistency. NoSQL archiving varies by data model, may use TTL (time-to-live) features, cold storage, or separate collections. SQL archiving more structured, NoSQL archiving more flexible but less standardized. Both reduce active dataset size and costs.

text: Explain the concept of API design for mobile applications.
idealAnswer: Mobile API design includes optimizing for bandwidth (minimize payload size), supporting offline functionality, implementing efficient pagination, using push notifications, and considering battery impact. Mobile APIs should be forgiving of network conditions, support background sync, and provide progressive data loading.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data compression?
idealAnswer: SQL databases offer built-in compression at table or column level, with various compression algorithms. NoSQL compression varies by implementation: some compress automatically, others require configuration. SQL compression more standardized, NoSQL compression depends on database type and configuration. Both reduce storage costs and improve I/O performance.

text: Explain the concept of API security for public APIs.
idealAnswer: Public API security includes API keys for authentication, rate limiting to prevent abuse, request signing for integrity, IP whitelisting, and monitoring for suspicious activity. Documentation should clearly communicate security requirements. Consider using API gateways for centralized security management and implement proper CORS policies.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data synchronization?
idealAnswer: SQL synchronization uses replication, log-based CDC (Change Data Capture), and ETL processes. NoSQL synchronization varies: some have built-in replication, others require custom sync logic. SQL synchronization more mature with established tools, NoSQL synchronization depends on database capabilities and may require custom solutions for complex scenarios.

text: Explain the concept of API design for IoT applications.
idealAnswer: IoT API design includes handling high device volumes, supporting lightweight protocols (MQTT, CoAP), implementing efficient data batching, managing device authentication at scale, and supporting offline operation. APIs should handle intermittent connectivity, provide device management endpoints, and optimize for low-bandwidth networks.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data governance?
idealAnswer: SQL data governance includes established practices for data quality, lineage, privacy, and compliance with tools and standards. NoSQL data governance is less mature, requiring custom approaches for different data models. SQL governance more mature with dedicated tools, NoSQL governance evolving with database adoption.

text: Explain the concept of API security for internal APIs.
idealAnswer: Internal API security includes network-level security (VPC, firewalls), service-to-service authentication (mTLS, JWT), principle of least privilege, regular security audits, and monitoring. While less exposed than public APIs, internal APIs still need proper authentication, authorization, and monitoring to prevent insider threats and lateral movement.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data masking?
idealAnswer: SQL data masking uses built-in features or third-party tools to mask sensitive data in non-production environments. NoSQL data masking varies by implementation, may require custom masking logic for different data models. SQL masking more standardized, NoSQL masking depends on database type and may require custom implementation.

text: Explain the concept of API design for real-time applications.
idealAnswer: Real-time API design includes using WebSockets or Server-Sent Events for push updates, implementing optimistic UI updates, handling connection failures gracefully, supporting reconnection logic, and minimizing latency. APIs should provide real-time endpoints alongside REST endpoints for different use cases.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data lineage?
idealAnswer: SQL data lineage tracked through database logs, ETL tools, and metadata repositories with established practices. NoSQL data lineage less standardized, requiring custom solutions for different data models. SQL lineage more mature with dedicated tools, NoSQL lineage evolving with database adoption and schema flexibility.

text: Explain the concept of microservices communication patterns.
idealAnswer: Microservices communicate via synchronous (REST, gRPC) or asynchronous (message queues, event streaming) patterns. Synchronous is simpler but creates coupling. Asynchronous provides decoupling and reliability. Service mesh handles communication complexity.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL when to use each?
idealAnswer: Use SQL when data structure is well-defined, relationships are complex, ACID transactions required. Use NoSQL when data structure is flexible or evolving, high write throughput needed, horizontal scaling required.

text: Explain the concept of API rate limiting.
idealAnswer: API rate limiting controls the number of requests a client can make in a time period. Prevents abuse, ensures fair usage, and protects system resources. Algorithms include token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window.

text: What is the difference between stateful and stateless applications?
idealAnswer: Stateful applications maintain client context between requests, harder to scale. Stateless applications don't maintain context, each request independent, easier to scale horizontally. Modern architectures favor stateless.

text: Explain the concept of database connection pooling.
idealAnswer: Connection pooling maintains a cache of database connections to reuse for multiple requests. Reduces overhead of creating new connections, improves performance. Pool size configuration balances performance and resource consumption.

text: What is the difference between monolithic and serverless architecture?
idealAnswer: Monolithic runs continuously on servers, you manage infrastructure. Serverless runs on-demand in functions, cloud manages infrastructure, pay-per-use. Monolithic for stable workloads, serverless for sporadic traffic.

text: Explain the concept of API versioning strategies.
idealAnswer: API versioning manages changes without breaking existing clients. Strategies include URL versioning, header versioning, query parameter versioning, and content negotiation. Each has trade-offs in caching and implementation.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data models?
idealAnswer: SQL uses relational model with tables, rows, columns, and predefined schemas. NoSQL offers various models: document, key-value, column-family, and graph. More flexible schemas, better for unstructured data.

text: Explain the concept of eventual consistency in distributed systems.
idealAnswer: Eventual consistency guarantees that if no new updates are made, eventually all accesses will return the last updated value. Used in distributed systems where immediate consistency is impractical. Trade-offs include temporary inconsistencies.

text: What is the difference between synchronous and asynchronous replication?
idealAnswer: Synchronous replication waits for acknowledgment from all replicas before confirming write, ensures strong consistency but slower performance. Asynchronous replication confirms write immediately, replicates in background, faster but risk of data loss.

text: Explain the concept of API authentication methods.
idealAnswer: API authentication methods include API keys, OAuth 2.0, JWT, Basic Auth, and mutual TLS. Choice depends on security requirements, use case, and implementation complexity. OAuth 2.0 and JWT are most common.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL scaling?
idealAnswer: SQL databases traditionally scale vertically, though some support horizontal scaling with complexity. NoSQL databases designed for horizontal scaling across commodity servers. SQL scaling limited by single-server constraints.

text: Explain the concept of database indexing strategies.
idealAnswer: Indexing strategies include B-tree indexes, hash indexes, composite indexes, covering indexes, and partial indexes. Choice depends on query patterns, read/write ratios, and storage constraints. Over-indexing slows writes.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL query languages?
idealAnswer: SQL uses standardized declarative language with JOINs for relational data. NoSQL query languages vary by type: document stores use JSON-like queries, key-value stores use simple key access. SQL is more standardized.

text: Explain the concept of API security best practices.
idealAnswer: API security best practices include using HTTPS, implementing proper authentication and authorization, rate limiting, input validation, output encoding, using security headers, and logging and monitoring.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL transaction support?
idealAnswer: SQL databases provide full ACID transaction support across multiple operations. NoSQL transaction support varies: some document databases support multi-document transactions, key-value stores often limited to single-key operations.

text: Explain the concept of API documentation tools.
idealAnswer: API documentation tools include Swagger/OpenAPI, Postman, API Blueprint, and RAML. Tools help create, maintain, and share API documentation, improving developer experience and API adoption.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL schema flexibility?
idealAnswer: SQL databases require predefined schema with fixed columns and types, schema changes are expensive. NoSQL databases offer schema flexibility, can store varying structures, evolve schema without downtime.

text: Explain the concept of API testing strategies.
idealAnswer: API testing strategies include unit testing, integration testing, contract testing, performance testing, and security testing. Tools include Postman, JMeter, SoapUI. Automated testing in CI/CD ensures API reliability.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data consistency models?
idealAnswer: SQL databases typically offer strong consistency. NoSQL databases offer various consistency models: strong, eventual, causal, and tunable consistency. Trade-offs between consistency, availability, and partition tolerance.

text: Explain the concept of API gateway patterns.
idealAnswer: API gateway patterns include single entry point, request routing, composition, protocol translation, and cross-cutting concerns. Simplifies client interaction, provides security, and handles traffic management.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL use cases?
idealAnswer: SQL use cases: financial systems, inventory management, CRM. NoSQL use cases: real-time big data, content management, social networks, IoT data. SQL for structured data, NoSQL for flexible data.

text: Explain the concept of API monitoring and observability.
idealAnswer: API monitoring tracks metrics, logging captures events, tracing follows requests across services. Tools include Prometheus, Grafana, ELK stack. Observability combines monitoring, logging, and tracing to understand system behavior.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL deployment models?
idealAnswer: SQL databases often deployed on dedicated servers or managed services with vertical scaling focus. NoSQL databases designed for distributed deployment across clusters, horizontal scaling, and cloud-native environments.

text: Explain the concept of API design principles.
idealAnswer: API design principles include using nouns for resources, consistent naming conventions, appropriate HTTP methods, status codes, pagination, filtering, sorting, versioning, and comprehensive documentation.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL backup and recovery?
idealAnswer: SQL backup typically involves full database dumps, transaction logs, point-in-time recovery. NoSQL backup varies: document stores use snapshots, key-value stores use key-level backup. SQL backup more standardized.

text: Explain the concept of API rate limiting algorithms.
idealAnswer: Rate limiting algorithms include token bucket, leaky bucket, fixed window, and sliding window. Choice depends on desired traffic shape, implementation complexity, and accuracy requirements.

text: Explain the concept of containerization and Docker.
idealAnswer: Containerization packages applications with dependencies into lightweight containers. Docker provides container runtime, images, and orchestration. Benefits include consistency across environments, resource efficiency, and faster deployment.

text: What is the difference between Docker and Kubernetes?
idealAnswer: Docker is a container runtime for building and running containers. Kubernetes is a container orchestration platform that manages, scales, and deploys containerized applications across clusters. Docker for containers, K8s for orchestration.

text: Explain the concept of CI/CD pipelines.
idealAnswer: CI/CD (Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment) automates building, testing, and deploying code. CI ensures code changes are tested automatically, CD automates deployment to production. Tools include Jenkins, GitLab CI, GitHub Actions.

text: What is the difference between monolithic and microservices architecture?
idealAnswer: Monolithic has all functionality in single deployable unit, simpler but harder to scale. Microservices break into small independent services, better scalability and fault isolation but increased complexity. Trade-offs in development and operations.

text: Explain the concept of load balancing algorithms.
idealAnswer: Load balancing algorithms include round robin, least connections, IP hash, and weighted distribution. Round robin distributes evenly, least connections sends to server with fewest active connections, IP hash ensures session persistence.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data modeling?
idealAnswer: SQL data modeling focuses on normalization, reducing redundancy, defining relationships through foreign keys. NoSQL data modeling emphasizes denormalization, embedding related data, optimizing for read/write patterns. SQL for integrity, NoSQL for performance.

text: Explain the concept of API security headers.
idealAnswer: API security headers include CORS, CSP, X-Frame-Options, X-Content-Type-Options, Strict-Transport-Security, and X-XSS-Protection. Headers protect against various web vulnerabilities and attacks like XSS, clickjacking, and MITM.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL maturity and stability?
idealAnswer: SQL databases are mature, stable, with proven reliability over decades. NoSQL databases are newer, rapidly evolving, with frequent updates. SQL for mission-critical stability, NoSQL for innovation and modern use cases.

text: Explain the concept of API versioning deprecation strategies.
idealAnswer: API version deprecation strategies include sunset headers, grace periods, migration guides, automatic redirects, and feature flags. Communication through documentation, email notifications, and status pages. Smooth deprecation requires planning.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL vendor lock-in?
idealAnswer: SQL has standard language and concepts, reducing vendor lock-in. NoSQL has less standardization, more vendor-specific features and query languages, increasing lock-in risk. SQL easier to migrate, NoSQL migration more challenging.

text: Explain the concept of API load testing.
idealAnswer: API load testing simulates expected traffic to measure performance, identify bottlenecks, and determine capacity. Tools include JMeter, Gatling, k6. Metrics include response time, throughput, error rates. Regular load testing ensures APIs handle production traffic.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data integrity?
idealAnswer: SQL databases enforce data integrity through constraints, validation rules, and transactions. NoSQL databases offer limited integrity enforcement, often relying on application-level validation. SQL for database-enforced integrity, NoSQL for application-managed integrity.

text: Explain the concept of API documentation standards.
idealAnswer: API documentation standards include OpenAPI/Swagger, API Blueprint, RAML, and JSON Schema. Standards enable documentation generation, client SDK creation, and API testing. Good documentation includes endpoints, parameters, responses, examples.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL query performance?
idealAnswer: SQL query performance optimized through indexes, query optimization, and execution plans. NoSQL query performance varies: key-value extremely fast for key lookups, document stores good for nested queries. SQL for complex queries, NoSQL for specific access patterns.

text: Explain the concept of API security testing.
idealAnswer: API security testing includes penetration testing, vulnerability scanning, authentication testing, input validation testing, and authorization testing. Tools include OWASP ZAP, Burp Suite. Regular security testing identifies vulnerabilities.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL horizontal scaling?
idealAnswer: SQL horizontal scaling achieved through sharding, read replicas, and clustering, but complex to implement. NoSQL designed for horizontal scaling with built-in sharding, replication, and automatic distribution. SQL scaling possible but requires expertise.

text: Explain the concept of API governance.
idealAnswer: API governance includes policies for API design, security, versioning, documentation, and lifecycle management. Ensures consistency across APIs, compliance with standards, and proper deprecation processes. Tools include API gateways and management platforms.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data relationships?
idealAnswer: SQL uses foreign keys to define relationships between tables, supports complex JOINs, enforces referential integrity. NoSQL handles relationships differently: document databases embed related data or use manual references. SQL for complex relationships, NoSQL for embedded or graph-based relationships.

text: Explain the concept of API mocking for development.
idealAnswer: API mocking simulates API responses for development and testing without real backend. Tools include Postman Mock Server, JSON Server, WireMock. Benefits include parallel development, testing edge cases, and offline development.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL backup complexity?
idealAnswer: SQL backup more standardized with well-established tools and procedures. NoSQL backup varies by database type and implementation, some require different approaches for different data models. SQL backup processes more mature.

text: Explain the concept of API lifecycle management.
idealAnswer: API lifecycle management includes planning, design, development, testing, deployment, versioning, monitoring, and deprecation. Each phase requires specific processes and tools. Proper lifecycle management ensures API quality and maintainability.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data migration?
idealAnswer: SQL data migration uses standardized ETL tools, schema mapping, and transformation scripts. NoSQL data migration varies by data model, may require custom transformation logic. SQL migration more standardized, NoSQL migration depends on database characteristics.

text: Explain the concept of API rate limiting implementation.
idealAnswer: Rate limiting implementation can be at API gateway, application level, or using reverse proxies. Storage options include in-memory (Redis), distributed caches, or databases. Considerations include distributed systems consistency and performance impact.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data validation?
idealAnswer: SQL databases provide built-in data validation through constraints, data types, and triggers. NoSQL databases offer limited built-in validation, often relying on application-level validation or document schema validation. SQL for database-enforced validation.

text: Explain the concept of API monitoring metrics.
idealAnswer: API monitoring metrics include request rate, response time (p50, p95, p99), error rate, throughput, latency distribution, and resource utilization. Custom metrics track business-specific KPIs. Metrics collection uses tools like Prometheus, Datadog.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data partitioning?
idealAnswer: SQL partitioning divides large tables into smaller pieces based on ranges, lists, or hashes. NoSQL partitioning (sharding) distributes data across servers based on shard keys. SQL partitioning within single database, NoSQL sharding across distributed systems.

text: Explain the concept of API security best practices for authentication.
idealAnswer: API authentication best practices include using industry-standard protocols (OAuth 2.0, OpenID Connect), implementing token expiration and refresh, using secure token storage, multi-factor authentication for sensitive operations, and regularly rotating secrets.

text: What is the difference between SQL and NoSQL data archiving?
idealAnswer: SQL data archiving moves old data to separate tables or databases, maintaining schema consistency. NoSQL archiving varies by data model, may use TTL features, cold storage, or separate collections. Both reduce active dataset size and costs.
